# xqisie

Detect the browser from a user agent string and send Internet Explorer visitors to a bundled
"your browser is too old" page. Ships as UMD (browser global + CommonJS) and as an ES module;
detection also works in Node.js, because a supplied UA string never touches `navigator`.

## Install

```sh
npm install xqisie
```

CDN, no build step:

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/xqisie@0.1.0/lib/xqisie.min.js"></script>
<!-- exposes window.xqisie -->
```

## Imports

```js
const xqisie = require('xqisie');          // CommonJS -> lib/xqisie.js (UMD)
import xqisie from 'xqisie';               // ESM      -> lib/xqisie-esm.mjs
import { check, goLink } from 'xqisie';    // named exports are the same two functions
```

Raw files stay reachable through the subpaths `xqisie/lib/*` and `xqisie/page/*`. No TypeScript
declarations are published.

## Exported API

- `check(userAgent?: string): 'Chrome' | 'IE' | 'Firefox' | 'Opera' | 'Safari' | ''`
  Returns the browser family, or `''` when nothing matches. Passing a string inspects that UA
  instead of the ambient one and **never reads `navigator`**, so it is server-safe.
- `goLink(url?: string): boolean`
  Sets `location.href` to `url` **only** when `check()` reports `'IE'`. Returns `true` when it
  navigated, `false` otherwise, and never throws: with no `location` (Node, Worker, a DOM-less
  sandbox) it reports `false` instead of raising.

Those two functions are the entire runtime API; the default export is `{ check, goLink }`.

## Return values and detection order

| UA contains | `check()` returns |
| --- | --- |
| `OPR/` or `Opera` | `'Opera'` |
| `Trident` or `MSIE` | `'IE'` |
| `Chrome` | `'Chrome'` |
| `Firefox` | `'Firefox'` |
| `Safari` | `'Safari'` |
| none of the above | `''` |

The order is part of the contract: Opera is tested before Chrome (its UA carries both) and
Safari last (nearly every WebKit UA contains `Safari`).

## Key options

- `userAgent` — default `navigator.userAgent`, or `''` where that is absent. A non-empty string
  wins over the ambient value.
- `url` — default `'../page/'`. Any string; the browser resolves it, so a relative value is
  relative to the current document. Prefer an absolute path in production.

## Typical use

Gate a page before the application boots:

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/xqisie@0.1.0/lib/xqisie.min.js"></script>
<script>
  xqisie.goLink('/browser-tip/');   // no-op in every browser except IE
</script>
```

Classify requests server-side:

```js
const http = require('http');
const xqisie = require('xqisie');

http.createServer((req, res) => {
  res.end('browser is: ' + (xqisie.check(req.headers['user-agent']) || 'unknown'));
}).listen(3000, 'localhost');
```

## Constraints

- **Five return values plus `''`.** Edge reports `'Chrome'` and iOS Chrome/Firefox report
  `'Safari'`; both are deliberate. Branch on the current five values only.
- Detection uses the `Trident`/`MSIE` substrings and never reads `navigator.appVersion`.
- `goLink()` redirects and returns a boolean; it renders nothing of its own.
- `page/` is a copy-paste tip page (`index.html`, `go.html`, a redirect shim, CSS and icons).
  Copy the whole directory: the internal asset links are relative. The shim reads `?url=` by
  name, accepts only `http:`/`https:` targets (`javascript:`, `data:` and protocol-relative
  values are refused), waits 886 ms, then calls `location.replace()`.
- Everything is ES5 on purpose, including the tip-page shim, because it must execute on the
  browsers it detects.
- The manifest sets no `"type": "module"`, so `require('xqisie')` keeps resolving to the UMD build.
